title: Write a technical proposal for real-time order status notifications
ideal_answer:
## Problem

Customers today learn about order status changes by refreshing the page or waiting for the daily email digest. For the 70% of traffic that's mobile, this is the wrong experience. We want push delivery to the active session and SMS for terminal states regardless of session.

Four constraints shape the solution: Order Service is legacy Java/Oracle with no owning team and a six-week integrator cycle for changes; no event bus and no infra budget for two quarters; the GDPR opt-in flag lives in the Customer App rather than Order Service; volume is ~51k status events per day (17k orders × ~3 changes).

## Options considered

**A. Stand up an event bus and have Order Service emit events.** Architecturally the right answer, but blocked on both new infra and Order Service changes. Rejected.

**B. Outbox table in Order Service, polled by Notification Service.** One small migration plus a write-site addition; still costs the six-week integrator cycle. Kept as a follow-up if option C strains.

**C. Notification Service polls Oracle directly.** Read-only credentials, an indexed scan of `order_status_history` on a 2–5 second interval, dispatch from Notification Service. Zero Order Service changes, zero new infrastructure. Recommended.

## Recommendation

Implement option C. Notification Service polls Oracle for changes, then dispatches over existing channels:

- **Online users** → publish to Redis pub/sub. The Customer App's WebSocket gateway already subscribes to Redis (live-cart feature), so it forwards the event without modification.
- **Offline users or terminal states** → SMS via Twilio. Phone numbers come from the same Oracle read; opt-in is checked against Notification Service's own store.
- **GDPR opt-in** moves from Customer App localStorage to Notification Service Postgres. The app posts it on next login. EU customers default to no SMS until the flag is confirmed.

Volume at ~0.6 events/sec average makes the polling load negligible on Oracle, and dispatch reuses code paths that already exist. Median push latency comes out at ~2.5s, p95 ~6s — both well inside budget given the current alternative is a 24-hour digest.

## Rollout

1. Notification Service: read-only Oracle credentials, poll loop with high-water-mark cursor, status-event persistence in its own Postgres.
2. Customer App: post the GDPR opt-in to Notification Service on login; background-migrate existing users.
3. WebSocket dispatch behind a feature flag for staff.
4. SMS dispatch behind a flag for opted-in users in one country.
5. General rollout. The daily email digest stays in place as a safety net for four weeks past GA.

Six weeks end-to-end.

## Risks

- **History table assumptions.** Polling assumes `order_status_history` is append-only with a monotonic timestamp. Confirm with the integrator in week 1; if false, fall back to polling the orders table directly with a diff.
- **SMS cost.** Worst case (every event becomes SMS) ~$1.5k/day. The channel rule — offline OR terminal AND opt-in — keeps realistic spend an order of magnitude below.
- **GDPR drift.** Until the opt-in flag is confirmed in Notification Service, EU customers receive no SMS. The email digest covers the gap.
- **Notification Service downtime.** Events remain in Oracle; on recovery, we resume from the high-water mark. Notifications are delayed, not lost.

## Out of scope

Native mobile push (Apple/Google) — web push via WebSocket only. International SMS template translation. UI changes to notification preferences beyond the existing toggle.
prompt:
We want to add real-time order status notifications for customers — push to our React app when on, SMS when offline or for terminal states. Today customers refresh the page or wait for a daily email digest. Write a proposal for how to deliver this.

Context:

- The order data lives in **Order Service**, a Java service on an on-prem cluster, on top of Oracle. The team that built it was disbanded last year; changes go through an external integrator on ~6-week cycles. Customer phone numbers live in an Oracle table inside Order Service.
- **Notification Service** (Node, k8s) is modern, actively maintained, owns its own Postgres + Redis, and currently sends emails. The team is fast-moving and welcomes new work.
- **Customer App** (React) is modern. Has a WebSocket connection to a thin gateway already (used by the live cart feature). Mobile is 70% of traffic.
- **No event bus** today. Services call each other via REST or read shared DB tables. No Kafka, no SQS, no NATS. Infra budget for the next two quarters is effectively zero — anything new has to ride existing platforms.
- **Compliance**: EU customers require explicit SMS opt-in (GDPR). The opt-in flag lives in the Customer App today and isn't synced to Order Service.
- Volume: ~17k orders/day, ~3 status changes per order on average.

Pick an approach and write up the proposal. Cover the problem, the options you considered, the recommendation with rationale, the rollout, and the main risks. Audience is the engineering org's tech leads (~10 people) — they'll read this and either approve or push back. Make decisions; don't punt with "it depends".
